title: Pissaladière
subtitle: Niçoise onion tart with anchovies and olives
excerpt: A Provençal flatbread or tart base covered with a thick layer of very slowly caramelised onions, anchovy fillets in a crosshatch, and black Niçoise olives. Rich, savoury, and deeply satisfying.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pissaladière (from the Niçoise dialect word pissalat, a fermented anchovy paste) is one of the signature dishes of Nice and the surrounding Côte d'Azur. It is related to the Italian focaccia and the Ligurian sardenaira (an anchovy flatbread from the border region between France and Italy). The base of pissaladière is traditionally a bread dough (sometimes an enriched olive oil dough) rather than a pastry case; the topping is a thick layer of onions that have been cooked in olive oil so slowly and for so long (45 minutes to 1 hour) that they collapse to a sweet, jammy, almost paste-like consistency. Pissalat (the fermented anchovy paste) has largely been replaced by anchovy fillets in oil. The anchovies are arranged in a diagonal crosshatch pattern over the onions, with a black olive pressed into each diamond. In Nice, pissaladière is sold from bakeries and eaten as a snack or first course.

recipeTools.notes: A large baking tray, approximately 30 x 40 cm.
A large, heavy-based frying pan for the onions.

content.text: The onions are the foundation and must be cooked until they are completely sweet, jammy, and collapsed: this takes a minimum of 45 minutes over a low-medium heat. They should be deeply golden-brown, not merely softened. Season lightly during cooking because the anchovies and olives provide abundant salt at the end. The bread dough base can be replaced with ready-made pizza dough or puff pastry for a quicker result, though the texture will differ.

items.preparation: 2 tbsp for the dough, 4 tbsp for the onions
in oil, drained; for the topping

content.text: Make the dough: mix the flour, yeast, and salt. Add 180 ml warm water and 2 tablespoons of olive oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled.

Cook the onions: heat 4 tablespoons of olive oil in a large, wide pan over medium-low heat. Add the onions, garlic, thyme, and bay with a pinch of salt. Cook for 45 to 55 minutes, stirring regularly, until deeply golden, sweet, and jammy. Remove the thyme and bay.

Heat the oven to 220 C / fan 200 C / gas 7. Oil a large baking tray. Stretch and press the dough across the tray to form a thin rectangle. Spread the caramelised onions over the surface, leaving a 1 cm border. Arrange the anchovy fillets in a crosshatch pattern. Press a black olive into each diamond. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until the base is golden and the topping is lightly browned. Serve warm or at room temperature.
